title: Storefront Customer API Boundary and Password Management Architecture
context: The storefront UI needs to access customer authentication, profile editing, and secure password changing. Customer data logic is currently hosted in admin-api, causing storefront-ui to call the admin port directly, which presents security and boundary concerns.

options_considered.option: Option A: Retain customer routes in admin-api (Port 8788) and make storefront-ui call the admin port directly.
pros: Faster MVP development: no need to migrate files or rebind database connections.
cons: Critical Security Boundary Issue: exposes the administrative API port to the public storefront/web traffic.
Violates the principle of least privilege and proper service segregation.

options_considered.option: Option B: Migrate all customer-facing routes (/auth/*, /customer/*) into public-api (Port 8787). Storefront-ui calls only public-api.
pros: Clean security boundary: administrative API (8788) can be closed to external public traffic.
Correct separation of concerns: public shopper traffic is handled by public-api, independent of admin operations.
Allows independent scaling and caching profiles at Cloudflare Edge.
cons: Requires shifting customer.ts, auth.ts, and middleware from admin-api to public-api.

decision: Adopt Option B. Migrate customer routes from admin-api to public-api. Storefront UI must only communicate with public-api (Port 8787). Enforce secure httpOnly cookies for session management with SameSite=Lax. In the new customer change-password endpoint, verify current password hash via PBKDF2 before updating, reject password reuse, and maintain current session cookie after update.

positive: Secures administrative API from direct exposure to storefront web clients.
Ensures clear service boundaries between administrative and customer operations.
Protects user passwords from timing attacks, dictionary reuse, and token exposure.
negative: Requires small effort to migrate and test Honos customerApp router in public-api.

migration_plan: 1. Move customerApp Hono router from admin-api/src/customer.ts to public-api/src/routes/customer.ts. 2. Bind CACHE_KV and DB to public-api Cloudflare Worker. 3. Update storefront API_BASE environment variable to point to port 8787. 4. Implement customer change-password endpoint in public-api.
rollback_plan: If public-api customer routing fails, fallback to admin-api customer routing by reverting the storefront API_BASE pointer back to 8788.
